---
date: "2026-09-12"
branch: tdd-implement/defense-ledger-proposed-components
status: in-progress
notes: "R/G TDD — residual-view live editing: update CLI, CLI-schema/parity metadata, client-side in-memory matrix editing, bidirectional import/export."
---

# TDD Implement — Residual View Live Editing

Orchestration skill: `tdd-implement`. Builds on milestone (a) from the prior
`view-and-serve` plan (static Dioxus-SSR render, merged in 9ad1ff3). Supersedes
that plan's milestones (b)-(f) (axum + dioxus-liveview server) — a live backend
is unnecessary for "purely visual, in-memory" edits; a client-side TS engine
regenerating the existing static DOM satisfies the requirement with far less
surface area, and keeps `residual view`'s output a single dependency-free HTML
file (per the existing `html_command_generator_does_not_mutate_the_ledger` /
no-fetch/no-WS invariant).

## Locked decisions

| Item | Decision |
|------|----------|
| Live backend | **Rejected.** No axum/dioxus-liveview server. All mutation is client-side, in-memory, against the snapshot already embedded in the page. |
| CLI parity mechanism | A hidden `residual internal cli-schema` command serializes clap's real `Command` tree (subcommand + arg flags) to JSON — not a hand-duplicated Rust struct. Single source of truth is `src/cli.rs` itself. |
| TS toolchain | `bun` (already present on the dev host; added explicitly to `flake.nix` devShell `packages` for reproducibility). `bun test` for TS unit/parity tests, `bun build` to produce the shipped bundle. |
| Shipped JS artifact | Compiled bundle (`src/view/generated/app.js`) is **checked into the repo**, not built during `cargo build`/crane's sandboxed derivation (no network/bun guaranteed there). Regenerated via `scripts/gen-view-bundle.sh`, run manually or in CI — not part of `residual verify all`. |
| `src/view/commands.rs` (`StagedAdd`, `format_add_command`) | **Dead code** — built for the abandoned live-server plan, never wired into `static_export.rs` or `cli.rs`. Deleted in Phase 8, not repurposed. |
| Update CLI shape | `residual update <type> --<id-flag> <id> [...same optional flags as add]`, plus repeatable `--add-component`/`--remove-component` on stressor/purpose updates (folds NKP mutation into `update`, superseding `add residue`/`remove residue` as the *generated*-command surface; those subcommands remain for direct CLI use). |
| Row/column ordering | Everywhere emitted or bucketed: components, attractors, personas, forces (stressors/purposes); all `update` commands ordered after all `add` commands. |
| Write-lock header | `residual write authorize` (existing `WriteOp::Authorize`, `src/cli.rs:44`), included only in the downloadable `.sh` script, never in the plain copy-to-clipboard text. |
| Tests | Colocated: Rust tests in `#[cfg(test)]` modules beside the code; TS tests as `*.test.ts` beside their source under `web/`. |

## Phase index

| # | Phase | Surface | Primary forces |
|---|-------|---------|-----------------|
| 0 | Environment scaffolding | `flake.nix`, `web/` skeleton | — |
| 1 | `residual update` CLI | `src/cli.rs`, `src/storage/*.rs` | A-08, P-30/P-31 pattern |
| 2 | CLI schema introspection | `src/cli.rs` (`internal cli-schema`) | A-19 (operator/agent parity trust) |
| 3 | TS import parser + parity tests | `web/src/import-parser.ts` | S-27, A-19 |
| 4 | In-memory model + validation | `web/src/model.ts` | S-26, A-06 |
| 5 | DOM/rendering integration | `web/src/render.ts`, `src/view/shell.html` | S-26, S-27, A-06 |
| 6 | Import modal UI | `web/src/import-modal.ts` | A-06 |
| 7 | Export (bash script) | `web/src/export.ts` | A-08 |
| 8 | Cleanup + wiring + integration | `static_export.rs`, `mod.rs`, delete `commands.rs` | — |

---

## Phase 0 — Environment scaffolding

**Modules:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/storage/{stressors,purposes,attractors,components,terminology,personas,residues}.rs`

| Surface | Behavior |
|---------|----------|
| `residual update stressor --force-id <id> [--description] [--attractor-id] [--naive-change] [--outcomes] [--add-component <id>]... [--remove-component <id>]...` | Patches only supplied fields; add/remove-component mutate the residues.csv row for that force id |
| `residual update purpose --force-id <id> [...same shape, --feature instead of --naive-change]` | ditto |
| `residual update attractor --id <id> [--name] [--positive-state] [--negative-state] [--description]` | ditto |
| `residual update component --name <id> [--description] [--status] [--architecture-set]` | ditto |
| `residual update term --term <id> [--definition]` | ditto |
| `residual update persona --name <id> [--role]` | ditto |

Idempotency/session-hash guards mirror existing `add`/`remove` commands. Unknown id → error, no partial writes.

**Colocated tests:** in each `src/storage/*.rs` module + `src/cli.rs` integration tests (tempdir pattern already used by `remove_residue_clears_matrix_cell` etc).

## Phase 2 — CLI schema introspection

Add a hidden top-level command (not shown in `--help`, e.g. `#[command(hide = true)]`) `residual internal cli-schema` that walks `Cli::command()` (clap's `Command` value, via `<Cli as CommandFactory>::command()`) and serializes: for `add`/`update` subcommands only, `{ subcommand: "add stressor", flags: [{ name, required, multiple, takes_value }] }`.

Red: unit test asserting the schema contains e.g. `"add stressor"` with a `--description` flag marked required, and `"update stressor"` with the same flag marked optional. Green: implement via clap introspection (no hand-listing).

`web/src/import-parser.ts`: tokenizes a pasted line (`residual add stressor --description "..." ...` / `residual update ...`) respecting shell quoting, maps flags to a typed pending-item, validates required flags against `cli-schema.json`. - `web/src/import-parser.test.ts` — hand-written cases per subcommand (happy path, missing required flag, unknown flag, quoting edge cases).
- `web/src/import-parser.parity.test.ts` — loads `cli-schema.json` and, for every documented subcommand/flag, asserts the parser's flag table recognizes it (loop over schema, not a hand-enumerated mirror) — this is the automatic parity mechanism; it fails the moment `cli-schema.json` is regenerated with a flag the parser doesn't know about.

## Phase 4 — In-memory model + validation

`web/src/model.ts`, framework-free pure functions/types:
- `PendingState`: adds + updates per bucket (components, attractors, personas, forces), plus in-memory NKP toggles keyed by force-id×component-id.
- Row validity: required-field-empty check per force type; force additionally invalid iff it has zero components toggled on.
- Ordering: stable bucket sort (components, attractors, personas, forces) with all updates ordered after all adds within/across buckets as specified.

`web/src/model.test.ts` covers validation edge cases and ordering.

Replaces the inline `<script>` in `src/view/shell.html` (currently only drives the below-table add forms) with the compiled bundle from `web/src/render.ts`, wired against `model.ts`:
- Right-click context menu → add row above/below (visual reorder only, no stored order) → new row opens in edit mode.
- Double-click on an NKP cell toggles it via `model.ts`.
- Row **Edit** button (no double-click) expands non-NKP fields → **OK**/**Cancel**; attractor field renders as `<select>` populated from the snapshot's attractors plus any added this session.
- Below-table component-add form appends an in-memory column; table re-renders.
- Two checkboxes: show/hide proposed components; show/hide components unrelated to the currently filtered forces.
- Red state: a CSS class distinct from the existing fusion/fission highlight class, applied to invalid cells and propagated to the sticky header cell (column) and sticky label cell (row) for any invalid cell's axis.

Pure "what should be tinted / what rows are valid" decisions stay in `model.ts` (unit-testable); `render.ts` only consumes that output to mutate the DOM — kept thin so it doesn't need a DOM-testing harness. Manual browser verification (`residual view`) closes this phase per the repo's UI-testing standard.

## Phase 6 — Import modal UI

`web/src/import-modal.ts`: modal with a primary paste textarea, an "Import" action running `import-parser.ts`, appending returned valid items into the existing `PendingState` (merge, not replace — `Clear` remains the reset action). On parse errors, offending lines move into a second textbox; a **Retry** button re-runs the parser against both boxes' concatenated content and moves newly-valid lines into the primary box.

## Phase 7 — Export (bash script)

`web/src/export.ts`: existing "Copy commands" behavior unchanged (uses `model.ts` output, no auth header). New "Generate bash script" button builds `#!/bin/env bash\n\nresidual write authorize\n\n<same ordered commands>` and triggers a `.sh` download via a Blob URL.

## Phase 8 — Cleanup + wiring + integration

- Delete `src/view/commands.rs`; remove its `pub use` from `src/view/mod.rs`.
- `static_export.rs` embeds `web/generated/app.js` (post-`gen-view-bundle.sh`) via `include_str!`, replacing the current inline script content in the rendered HTML.
- Full suite: `cargo test`, `bun test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- --deny warnings` (existing pre-existing warnings excluded per prior session's baseline), `residual verify all`, manual `residual view` smoke test in a browser.

```json
]}
```

```ts
export interface ParseError { line: string; message: string; }
```

- An unrecognized subcommand (e.g. `residual add nonsense ...`) → a `ParseError`.
- A line that isn't a `residual` invocation at all → a `ParseError` with a clear message (e.g. "not a residual add/update command").

1. `tokenizeCommandLine(line: string): string[]` — split on whitespace outside double quotes; strip the surrounding quotes from quoted tokens; unescape `\"` to `"` inside them. 2. `getKnownFlags(subcommand: string): KnownFlag[] | undefined` — load `cli-schema.json`, find the matching `{ subcommand, flags }` entry, map its `flags` array (each `{ name, required, multiple }`) to `KnownFlag[]`.

   - Tokenize it.
   - Expect the shape `residual <add|update> <type> --flag value...` (check the test file for exactly how strict this needs to be — e.g. does it require the literal word `residual` as token 0? what happens with leading/trailing whitespace?).
   - Look up `getKnownFlags(\`${addOrUpdate} ${type}\`)`; if `undefined`, produce a `ParseError` for that line (message should mention it's an unrecognized subcommand — match whatever wording the test asserts, likely via a substring match, not exact-string).

For a flag not in the known-flags list, produce a `ParseError` mentioning the flag name.    - After consuming all tokens, check every `required: true` known flag was supplied (in `fields` or as a non-empty `multipleFields` entry, per what the tests expect for required-and-multiple combos, if any exist) — if not, produce a `ParseError` naming the missing flag(s).
   - On success, push a `PendingItem` with `kind`, `type`, `fields`, `multipleFields`, and `raw` (the original line text, per the type contract — confirm from the test file).
   - A line that isn't a `residual add/update ...` invocation at all → a `ParseError` with a message indicating that (check exact expected substring in the test).

## Constraints

- Don't touch the two test files or `web/generated/cli-schema.json` unless you find a genuine bug in a test's expectation (if so, explain why in your report; this should be rare/unlikely since the red-phase agent wrote these against the real schema).
- Keep the implementation "relatively simple" per the project's own framing — this is explicitly meant to be a lightweight parser, not a full shell grammar. Don't add features beyond what the tests require.
- Strict TypeScript per `web/tsconfig.json` — avoid `any`; use proper types throughout.

## When done

Run `nix develop -c bun test web/src` and confirm 0 failures, 40/40 passing (or however many tests actually exist — just confirm full green, no skips). Report: the final `import-parser.ts` source (paste it in full), the test output, and any deviations from the plan above with justification. Keep prose under 400 words plus raw output and the pasted source.

input.prompt:
You are a red-phase subagent in an R/G TDD workflow. Repo: /home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual, branch tdd-implement/defense-ledger-proposed-components. Run tests with `nix develop -c bun test web/src` from repo root. Write ONLY failing tests — no implementation logic. Stub functions should `throw new Error("not yet implemented — green phase")`.

## Background

This is `residual view`'s live-editing feature. Read `/home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual/residual/iterations/view-live-editing-plan.md` in full first — it's the governing plan for this whole feature arc (Phase 4 in that plan is what you're doing now). Also read `/home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual/web/src/import-parser.ts` (just landed, Phase 3) to see the existing `PendingItem`/`ParseError`/`ParseResult` shapes and code style you should stay consistent with (same repo, same conventions: strict TS, JSDoc comments on exported members, no `any`).

Also skim `/home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual/src/view/snapshot.rs` (Rust) to see the shape of `LandscapeSnapshot` (attractors, stressors, purposes, components, residues, defense) that gets embedded as JSON into the rendered HTML page (`residual-snapshot` script tag) — your TS model needs a rough TS mirror of the relevant parts (attractors: id/name/positive_state/negative_state; components: name/description/status/architecture_set; forces (stressors+purposes): id/description/attractor_id/naive_change-or-feature/outcomes; residues: which force×component cells are coupled) since validation needs to reason over "does this row have any component toggled on."

## What to build: `web/src/model.ts` + `web/src/model.test.ts`

This is a framework-free, DOM-free, pure-functions-and-types module representing the live-editing state on top of a loaded snapshot. It does NOT touch the DOM (that's Phase 5, someone else's job later) and does NOT do the CLI-text parsing (that's `import-parser.ts`, already done) — it's the layer *between* them: the in-memory "what has the user added/changed/toggled" state plus validation plus the final "turn this into `residual add/update` command-line text" step.

### Types to define

- `SnapshotAttractor { id: string; name: string; positiveState: string; negativeState: string }`
- `SnapshotComponent { name: string; description: string; status: "proposed" | "actual"; architectureSet: string }`
- `SnapshotForce { id: string; kind: "stressor" | "purpose"; description: string; attractorId: string; naiveChangeOrFeature: string; outcomes: string; shortname: string; components: string[] /* component names currently coupled via residues.csv */ }`
- A `PendingState` representing everything added/changed this session, on top of a base snapshot:
  ```ts
  interface PendingState {
    baseAttractors: SnapshotAttractor[];
    baseComponents: SnapshotComponent[];
    baseForces: SnapshotForce[];
    addedAttractors: SnapshotAttractor[];   // in-memory, not yet in base
    addedComponents: SnapshotComponent[];
    addedForces: (SnapshotForce & { tempId: string })[]; // new rows, no real force id yet
    updatedForces: Record<string, Partial<Omit<SnapshotForce, "id" | "kind">> & { components?: string[] }>; // keyed by real force id OR tempId
    // (your call on exact shape for personas/terms if you think they belong here per the plan — the plan says non-table forms (attractors/terms/personas) stay below-table but attractors specifically need to appear in a dropdown per the plan, so at minimum attractors need "added this session" tracking; terms/personas can be a simpler bucket if you think they need any state at all beyond what import-parser already produces — use your judgment and document it)
  }
  ```
  Adjust field names/shape as you see fit — the above is a starting sketch, not gospel. Keep it something a DOM layer could reasonably consume later.

### Functions to define (all real logic deferred to green phase — stub with `throw new Error("not yet implemented — green phase")`)

1. **Validation** — per the plan's rules:
   - `isForceValid(force, requiredFieldsForKind): boolean` (or similar) — a force (added or updated-in-place) is invalid if any required field is empty, OR if it has zero components toggled on ("no components selected is invalid"). Required fields per the plan: stressor needs description, attractor-id, naive-change, outcomes; purpose needs description, attractor-id, feature (naive_change), outcomes — mirror exactly what `residual add stressor`/`residual add purpose` require (check `web/generated/cli-schema.json` for `"add stressor"`/`"add purpose"` — flags marked `required: true` there ARE the required-fields ground truth; use that instead of hand-guessing).
   - A function that computes validity for the WHOLE current state, returning something like `{ invalidForceIds: Set<string>, invalidCellsByForce: Record<string, string[]> }` or similar (your call) — needed later for red-highlighting which cells/rows/sticky headers to tint.

2. **Ordering** — a function `orderedEntries(state: PendingState)` (or similar) that returns a flat, deterministically ordered list of "things to emit as commands", following the plan's fixed rule: components, then attractors, then personas (if modeled here), then forces (stressors/purposes) — and within that, ALL additions across every bucket before ALL updates across every bucket. Write tests asserting this exact bucket+add/update ordering with a mixed fixture (e.g. an added component, an added attractor, an added stressor, an updated stressor, an updated attractor — assert the resulting order is: added component, added attractor, added stressor, updated attractor, updated stressor — or whatever the precise plan-consistent order is; re-read the plan's "Ordering" section to get this exactly right, it says "all update commands ordered after all add commands").

3. **Command-line generation** — `toCommandLines(state: PendingState): { line: string; valid: boolean }[]` (or similar) — for each ordered entry, render the equivalent `residual add <type> --flag "value" ...` / `residual update <type> --force-id <id> ...` text (mirror the existing `--flag value` shell-quoting style already used in `import-parser.ts`'s inverse direction — quote every value in double quotes, escaping embedded `"` as `\"`, to round-trip with the parser). Mark `valid: false` for lines belonging to an invalid force (per rule 1) — the DOM layer will comment these out with `# ` later, but that's Phase 5's job; this function's job is just to say which lines are valid vs not, alongside the line text itself (a Phase-5 caller can decide whether to prefix `# `). Write tests asserting invalid rows are flagged and valid rows aren't, and that flag ordering/quoting round-trips correctly through `parseImportText` from `import-parser.ts` (i.e. write at least one test that generates a command line via your function and re-parses it with `parseImportText`, asserting the parsed fields match the original — this is a good sanity/parity check between the two directions).

## Constraints

- Pure functions/types only — no DOM APIs (`document`, `window`, etc.), no side effects, no network.
- Strict TS, no `any`.
- Colocated `web/src/model.test.ts` beside `web/src/model.ts`.
- Don't modify `import-parser.ts` or its tests — only import from it (its exports are stable now, Phase 3 is done and committed).

## Verify before finishing

Run `nix develop -c bun test web/src` and confirm:
1. The 40 pre-existing import-parser tests still pass unchanged.
2. Your new model tests exist and FAIL via the intended `todo`/throw stubs (not compile errors, not wrong-reason failures).
Report: files created, the full type definitions you settled on (paste them), a short list of test names added, and the `bun test` tail output. Keep prose under 400 words plus pasted types/output.

## Current state (red, confirmed)

`web/src/model.ts` has types and stub functions (`isForceValid`, `computeStateValidity`, `orderedEntries`, `toCommandLines`) all throwing `new Error("not yet implemented — green phase")`. `web/src/model.test.ts` has the full test suite. `nix develop -c bun test web/src` currently shows 40 pass (pre-existing import-parser tests, untouched, do not break these) and 19 fail (all via the intended stub throw).

Read `web/src/model.ts` and `web/src/model.test.ts` in full yourself first — every type and every test assertion — before writing any implementation. Also read `web/src/import-parser.ts` (Phase 3, already done, stable) since `toCommandLines` output must round-trip through its `parseImportText` for several tests.

## IMPORTANT: a correctness fix already applied to the test file — read this before implementing `toCommandLines`

I (the parent orchestrating this TDD loop) personally reviewed the red-phase tests and found a real bug in the original design, which I already corrected directly in `model.test.ts` — implement to match the corrected tests, not any other assumption:

**The problem:** `residual add stressor` (and `add purpose`) has NO `--force-id` flag. The id is auto-generated server-side and only appears in stdout on success (`Added stressor S-61`). So when a user adds a brand-new stressor row in the UI AND toggles some NKP components on for it in the same session, the generated script cannot do `residual update stressor --force-id <tempId> --add-component ...` — `<tempId>` (e.g. `"NEW-1"`) is a UI-only bookkeeping key, not a real id, and that command would fail when actually run.

**The fix (already encoded in the test file):** when an added force has `components.length > 0`, `toCommandLines` must emit TWO lines instead of one:
1. A shell-variable-capture line wrapping the `add` invocation, e.g.:
   `NEW_1_ID=$(residual add stressor --description "d" --attractor-id "A-01" --naive-change "n" | ...)`
   — where `...` is whatever mechanism extracts the real id from stdout (e.g. `grep -oE '[A-Z]+-[0-9]+' | tail -1`, or similar — your call on the exact extraction command, the test doesn't pin down the interior of the `$(...)`, only that it starts with `<VARNAME>=$(residual add stressor` and ends with `)`). The variable name is derived from the tempId: sanitize by uppercasing and replacing every non-alphanumeric run with `_`, then suffix `_ID` — e.g. tempId `"NEW-1"` → `NEW_1_ID`. Check the exact test assertion in `model.test.ts` (search for `"an added force's real id is not known until"`) for the precise expected string.
2. A synthetic update line referencing that shell variable via `"$VARNAME"`, e.g.:
   `residual update stressor --force-id "$NEW_1_ID" --add-component "cli"`
   — check the exact test assertion for the precise expected string (search the same test).

When an added force has `components.length === 0`, it stays a single plain, unwrapped `residual add stressor --description "..." ...` line (no capture, no synthetic update) — see the other `toCommandLines` tests using empty `components: []`.

This synthetic capture-line pattern is intentionally NOT expected to round-trip through `parseImportText` (it's a shell scripting construct, not a plain CLI invocation) — don't try to make `parseImportText` understand it; that's out of scope.

For everything else (added attractors/components/terms/personas with no id-dependency problem, and UPDATES to forces/attractors/components that already have a real, known id from the base snapshot), lines are plain, directly `parseImportText`-parseable `residual add ...` / `residual update ...` invocations exactly as originally designed — no capture-wrapper needed since their identity is already known.

## What to implement

1. **`isForceValid`**: required fields per `web/generated/cli-schema.json`'s `add stressor`/`add purpose` entries (flags marked `required: true`) — check the test `"empty outcomes does NOT invalidate — outcomes is required:false in cli-schema.json"` to confirm outcomes is excluded. Also invalid if `components.length === 0` (zero components toggled).
2. **`computeStateValidity`**: walks base forces (with any pending update applied on top) and added forces, returning `{ invalidForceIds: Set<string>, invalidReasonsByForce: Record<string, string[]> }` keyed by real id for base forces or tempId for added forces — read the tests for exact reason-string expectations (e.g. `"attractorId"` appearing in the reasons array).
3. **`orderedEntries`**: bucket order component → attractor → persona → term → force; ALL adds (across every bucket, in that bucket order) before ALL updates (across every bucket, in that same bucket order). An added force with components gets TWO entries: `{ bucket: "force", action: "add", key: tempId }` then `{ bucket: "force", action: "update", key: tempId }` (the synthetic one) — read the ordering test carefully for exact placement of that synthetic update entry relative to other real updates.
4. **`toCommandLines`**: renders every ordered entry as command-line text per the correctness fix above, quoting every flag value in double quotes with `\"`-escaping for embedded quotes (mirror `import-parser.ts`'s `tokenizeCommandLine` unescaping so values round-trip exactly), marking `valid: false` for any line belonging to a force that fails `isForceValid`/`computeStateValidity`. For update lines (real ids), only emit flags for fields that are actually present in the pending update object (partial diff) plus `--add-component`/`--remove-component` for any component-list diff against the base force's `components` — read the `"an updated base force's component diff..."` test for exact expected diffing behavior (which components count as newly-added vs newly-removed).

## Constraints

- Don't modify `model.test.ts`, `import-parser.ts`, or `web/generated/cli-schema.json` — implement against them as fixed ground truth. If you believe there's still a genuine bug in a test after all this, stop and explain in your report rather than silently working around it.
- Strict TS, no `any`.
- Keep `model.ts`'s existing type definitions as-is unless a test literally cannot pass without a shape change — prefer adapting your implementation to the existing types.

## When done

Run `nix develop -c bun test web/src` and confirm 59/59 passing (0 failures), with the pre-existing 40 import-parser tests still green. Report: the full `model.ts` implementation (paste the four functions), the test tail output, and confirm explicitly that no generated line ever uses a tempId as a literal `--force-id` value. Keep prose under 400 words plus pasted code/output.

You are a red-phase subagent in an R/G TDD workflow. Repo: /home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual, branch tdd-implement/defense-ledger-proposed-components. Run tests with `nix develop -c bun test web/src` from repo root. Write ONLY failing tests — no implementation. Stub functions should `throw new Error("not yet implemented — green phase")`.

## Background

Read `/home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual/residual/iterations/view-live-editing-plan.md` in full (Phase 5 is what you're doing now — a sub-slice of it). Read `/home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual/web/src/model.ts` in full (Phase 4, done, stable — `PendingState`, `computeStateValidity`, `SnapshotComponent`, `SnapshotForce`, `SnapshotAttractor`, etc.) since this phase builds directly on it.

This is `residual view`'s live-editing UI. The existing rendered page (`src/view/shell.html`, already has a matrix `<table class="matrix">` rendered server-side via Dioxus-SSR with sticky header row (`thead th`, sticky top) and sticky first column (`.sticky-col`, sticky left) — read that file's `<style>` block, roughly lines 140-240, to see existing conventions: `[data-residue-cell][data-coupled="1"]` for a coupled NKP cell, `th[data-fission="1"]`/`td[data-fission="1"]` (amber outline, `var(--warn)` = `#c45c5c`, a muted red-orange) and `th[data-fusion="1"]`/`td[data-fusion="1"]` (`var(--coupled)` = `#c4a35a`, gold) for fusion/fission candidate highlighting.

## Your job: pure, DOM-free "what should be visually marked" decision logic

This is explicitly the part of Phase 5 that stays unit-testable (per the plan: "Pure 'what should be tinted / what rows are valid' decisions stay in model.ts-adjacent code; render.ts only consumes that output to mutate the DOM"). You are NOT writing DOM manipulation, event handlers, or HTML — just pure functions that take a `PendingState` (plus small config objects) and return plain data describing what should be visually marked, which a later (untested, DOM-wiring) phase will consume.

Create `web/src/render-decisions.ts` (stub) + `web/src/render-decisions.test.ts` (real tests) covering:

1. **Invalid-cell/row/sticky-axis marking.** Given a `PendingState`, compute, for every force (base+update-merged, and added), whether it's invalid (reuse `computeStateValidity` from `model.ts` — import it, don't reimplement), and derive:
   - Which force keys (real id or tempId) need their row's sticky label cell marked invalid.
   - Which component names need their column's sticky header cell marked invalid — a component's header is marked invalid if ANY currently-invalid force is invalid specifically because it has zero components (i.e., every component column shares the "blame" when a row fails purely on the "no components selected" rule) OR... actually think about this: per the spec, "if row 3's Feature column is invalid, row 3's sticky label AND the Feature column header both go red" — this is about a specific INVALID CELL (a specific force × field, e.g. an empty required text field isn't a matrix cell though — text fields like description/feature aren't NKP matrix columns at all, they're the row's own non-NKP data with no column in the grid). Re-read the original task spec carefully (it's summarized in the plan's "Validation" section) and use your judgment: the sticky-row/column double-marking rule most concretely applies to the NKP matrix itself — i.e., when a force has zero components toggled (the "no components selected is invalid" rule), which doesn't point at any *specific* component column since none are toggled. Given that ambiguity, design a `computeInvalidMarks(state): { invalidForceKeys: Set<string>; invalidComponentColumns: Set<string> }` where `invalidComponentColumns` is populated only by a DIFFERENT, more literal case your tests should define: if a specific NKP cell (force × component) is in some kind of "should be on but isn't sufeld" state — actually, simplify: since there is no per-cell required/optional concept in this NKP matrix (a cell is just coupled or not), the only realistic per-column invalid-marking case is "zero components toggled for this force" — which doesn't implicate one column over another. So: write your tests to assert `invalidComponentColumns` stays EMPTY for the "zero components" case (document this explicitly in a test name/comment explaining why), and instead make sure `invalidForceKeys` correctly includes both (a) forces failing required-text-field validation and (b) forces failing the zero-components rule. This is a deliberate, documented scope-narrowing versus a literal per-cell reading of the spec — explain your reasoning in a code comment.

2. **Visibility filtering for components** — `visibleComponents(state, options: { showProposed: boolean; showUnrelated: boolean; filteredForceIds: string[] | null }): string[]` (component names, in a stable order) where:
   - If `showProposed` is false, components with `status === "proposed"` (checking both `state.baseComponents` and `state.addedComponents`) are excluded.
   - If `showUnrelated` is false, a component is excluded unless at least one force among `filteredForceIds` (or ALL forces, base+added, if `filteredForceIds` is `null` meaning "no filter active") has that component in its (base-merged-with-pending-update) `components` list. Reuse whatever merging logic `model.ts` already has (check if it's exported, e.g. via `computeStateValidity`'s internals — if the merge logic isn't exported, write a small local helper in `render-decisions.ts` rather than duplicating `model.ts` internals verbatim; use your judgment, but don't reimplement isForceValid's business rules, just the base+update merge).

3. **Attractor dropdown options** — `attractorOptions(state): { id: string; name: string }[]` — merges `state.baseAttractors` with `state.addedAttractors` (attractors added this session, not yet in the base snapshot), sorted by name, so the UI's attractor `<select>` includes both.

## Constraints

- Pure functions/types only, no DOM APIs.
- Import from `./model.ts` for anything already defined there (`PendingState`, `computeStateValidity`, snapshot types) — don't redefine or duplicate those types.
- Strict TS, no `any`.
- Stub bodies throw `new Error("not yet implemented — green phase")`.

## Verify before finishing

Run `nix develop -c bun test web/src` and confirm:
1. The 60 pre-existing tests (import-parser + model) still pass unchanged.
2. Your new tests fail via the intended stub throw, not compile errors.
Report: files created, full type/function signatures, test names added, and the `bun test` tail output. Include your reasoning for the `invalidComponentColumns` scoping decision explicitly. Keep prose under 400 words plus signatures/output.

```ts
export function visibleComponents(state: PendingState, options: VisibilityOptions): string[] {
```
```ts
  const all = [...state.baseComponents, ...state.addedComponents];
  const filtered = options.showProposed ? all : all.filter((c) => c.status !== "proposed");

  if (options.showUnrelated) {
    return filtered.map((c) => c.name);
  }

  const relevantBaseForces = state.baseForces.filter(
    (f) => options.filteredForceIds === null || options.filteredForceIds.includes(f.id),
  );
  const relevantAddedForces = state.addedForces.filter(
    (f) => options.filteredForceIds === null || options.filteredForceIds.includes(f.tempId),
  );

  const relatedComponentNames = new Set<string>();
  for (const base of relevantBaseForces) {
    const update = state.updatedForces[base.id];
    const components = update?.components ?? base.components;
    for (const name of components) relatedComponentNames.add(name);
  }
  for (const added of relevantAddedForces) {
    for (const name of added.components) relatedComponentNames.add(name);
  }

  return filtered.filter((c) => relatedComponentNames.has(c.name)).map((c) => c.name);
}

export function attractorOptions(state: PendingState): AttractorOption[] {
```

   - For an ADDED force: mutate `addedForces[i].components` directly (add or remove `componentName`), no `updatedForces` entry involved (added forces aren't "updates", they don't exist yet).

2. **`addForceRow(state: PendingState, kind: "stressor" | "purpose"): PendingState`** — appends a new `AddedForce` to `addedForces` with a freshly generated unique `tempId` (e.g. `"NEW-1"`, `"NEW-2"`, ... — pick a generation scheme that can't collide with existing tempIds already in `state.addedForces`; test adding two rows in a row and assert distinct tempIds), all text fields empty (`""`), `components: []`, and the given `kind`. Return both the new state AND the generated tempId somehow — since the DOM layer will need to know which row it just created to open it in edit mode. Design the return type as `{ state: PendingState; tempId: string }` (adjust `addForceRow`'s signature/return type accordingly — your call on exact shape, just be consistent and document it).

3. **`updateForceField(state: PendingState, forceKey: string, field: "description" | "attractorId" | "naiveChangeOrFeature" | "outcomes" | "shortname", value: string): PendingState`** — for a base force id, sets `updatedForces[id][field] = value` (creating the update entry if absent, preserving other already-set fields on it). For an added-force tempId, sets the field directly on the matching entry in `addedForces` (mutate that field in a copied object, not the original array/object). Test both base and added-force paths, and test that setting a SECOND field afterward doesn't clobber the first (i.e. two sequential `updateForceField` calls on a base force accumulate into the same `updatedForces[id]` entry).

4. **`addComponentColumn(state: PendingState, component: { name: string; description: string; status: "proposed" | "actual"; architectureSet: string }): PendingState`** — appends to `addedComponents`. Test duplicate-name rejection: if `component.name` already exists in `baseComponents` or `addedComponents`, throw a clear `Error` (not silently ignore, not silently overwrite) — write a test asserting this throws.

5. **`addAttractorOption(state: PendingState, attractor: { id: string; name: string; description: string; positiveState: string; negativeState: string }): PendingState`** — appends to `addedAttractors`, same duplicate-id rejection behavior as above (throws).

## Constraints

- Pure, immutable, DOM-free. No `any`. Strict TS.
- Don't modify `model.ts`, `model.test.ts`, `render-decisions.ts`, or their tests — only import types from `model.ts`.
- Stub bodies: `throw new Error("not yet implemented — green phase")`.

## Verify before finishing

Run `cd web && nix develop /home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual -c bun test` and confirm:
1. The 75 pre-existing tests (import-parser, model, render-decisions) still pass unchanged.
2. Your new tests fail via the intended stub throw, not compile errors.
Report: files created, full function signatures with your chosen return-type designs, the specific behavior you pinned for the "toggle a base force's component back to its original state" question in point 1, and the `bun test` tail output. Keep prose under 400 words plus signatures/output.

```ts
// Pure reducer layer for the live-editing DOM to call into: takes a
// PendingState (see model.ts) and a user action's arguments, returns a NEW
// PendingState. No DOM, no mutation of the input state.
// ... (doc comments unchanged from stub) ...

import type { AddedForce, PendingState, SnapshotAttractor, SnapshotComponent } from "./model";

function sameElements(a: readonly string[], b: readonly string[]): boolean {
  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
  const sortedA = [...a].sort();
  const sortedB = [...b].sort();
  return sortedA.every((value, index) => value === sortedB[index]);
}

function toggled(components: readonly string[], name: string): string[] {
  return components.includes(name) ? components.filter((c) => c !== name) : [...components, name];
}

export function toggleComponent(state: PendingState, forceKey: string, componentName: string): PendingState {
  const addedIndex = state.addedForces.findIndex((f) => f.tempId === forceKey);
  if (addedIndex !== -1) {
    const target = state.addedForces[addedIndex]!;
    const nextForce: AddedForce = { ...target, components: toggled(target.components, componentName) };
    const nextAddedForces = [...state.addedForces];
    nextAddedForces[addedIndex] = nextForce;
    return { ...state, addedForces: nextAddedForces };
  }

  const base = state.baseForces.find((f) => f.id === forceKey);
  if (base === undefined) return state;

  const existingUpdate = state.updatedForces[forceKey];
  const effective = existingUpdate?.components ?? base.components;
  const nextComponents = toggled(effective, componentName);

  const nextUpdatedForces = { ...state.updatedForces };

  if (sameElements(nextComponents, base.components)) {
    if (existingUpdate === undefined) return state;
    const { components: _components, ...rest } = existingUpdate;
    if (Object.keys(rest).length === 0) {
      delete nextUpdatedForces[forceKey];
    } else {
      nextUpdatedForces[forceKey] = rest;
    }
  } else {
    nextUpdatedForces[forceKey] = { ...existingUpdate, components: nextComponents };
  }

  return { ...state, updatedForces: nextUpdatedForces };
}

export function addForceRow(
  state: PendingState,
  kind: "stressor" | "purpose",
): { state: PendingState; tempId: string } {
  let maxN = 0;
  for (const f of state.addedForces) {
    const match = /^NEW-(\d+)$/.exec(f.tempId);
    if (match) {
      const n = Number(match[1]);
      if (n > maxN) maxN = n;
    }
  }
  const tempId = `NEW-${maxN + 1}`;
  const newForce: AddedForce = {
    tempId, kind, description: "", attractorId: "", naiveChangeOrFeature: "",
    outcomes: "", shortname: "", components: [],
  };
  return { state: { ...state, addedForces: [...state.addedForces, newForce] }, tempId };
}

export function updateForceField(
  state: PendingState,
  forceKey: string,
  field: "description" | "attractorId" | "naiveChangeOrFeature" | "outcomes" | "shortname",
  value: string,
): PendingState {
  const addedIndex = state.addedForces.findIndex((f) => f.tempId === forceKey);
  if (addedIndex !== -1) {
    const target = state.addedForces[addedIndex]!;
    const nextForce: AddedForce = { ...target, [field]: value };
    const nextAddedForces = [...state.addedForces];
    nextAddedForces[addedIndex] = nextForce;
    return { ...state, addedForces: nextAddedForces };
  }
  const existingUpdate = state.updatedForces[forceKey];
  return { ...state, updatedForces: { ...state.updatedForces, [forceKey]: { ...existingUpdate, [field]: value } } };
}

export function addComponentColumn(state: PendingState, component: SnapshotComponent): PendingState {
  const exists = state.baseComponents.some((c) => c.name === component.name) ||
    state.addedComponents.some((c) => c.name === component.name);
  if (exists) throw new Error(`component "${component.name}" already exists`);
  return { ...state, addedComponents: [...state.addedComponents, component] };
}

export function addAttractorOption(state: PendingState, attractor: SnapshotAttractor): PendingState {
  const exists = state.baseAttractors.some((a) => a.id === attractor.id) ||
    state.addedAttractors.some((a) => a.id === attractor.id);
  if (exists) throw new Error(`attractor "${attractor.id}" already exists`);
  return { ...state, addedAttractors: [...state.addedAttractors, attractor] };
}
```

export function addForceRow(
  state: PendingState,
  kind: "stressor" | "purpose",
): { state: PendingState; tempId: string } {
  let maxN = 0;
  for (const f of state.addedForces) {
    const match = /^NEW-(\d+)$/.exec(f.tempId);
    if (match) {
      const n = Number(match[1]);
      if (n > maxN) maxN = n;
    }
  }
  const tempId = `NEW-${maxN + 1}`;
  const newForce: AddedForce = {
    tempId, kind, description: "", attractorId: "", naiveChangeOrFeature: "",
    outcomes: "", shortname: "", components: [],
  };
  return { state: { ...state, addedForces: [...state.addedForces, newForce] }, tempId };
}

export function updateForceField(
  state: PendingState,
  forceKey: string,
  field: "description" | "attractorId" | "naiveChangeOrFeature" | "outcomes" | "shortname",
  value: string,
): PendingState {
  const addedIndex = state.addedForces.findIndex((f) => f.tempId === forceKey);
  if (addedIndex !== -1) {

    const nextForce: AddedForce = { ...target, [field]: value };
    const nextAddedForces = [...state.addedForces];

- A button opens a modal with a primary paste `<textarea>`.

### Part A: state-merging (pure, no DOM)

Design `mergeImportedItems`'s return type accordingly and test the unmergeable-item case explicitly.

### Part B: DOM wiring for the modal

Design `mountImportModal(container: HTMLElement, getState: () => PendingState, setState: (next: PendingState) => void, options?: { onChange?: () => void }): void` attaching to a fixture container with (design this markup yourself, document it in a header comment, keep it simple):

- An "Import" action button that runs `parseImportText` on the primary textarea, splits lines into successfully-parsed vs errored, moves errored lines' raw text into the errors textarea (removing them from the primary textarea's displayed value), calls `mergeImportedItems` on the successfully-parsed items and `setState`s the merged result, and calls `options?.onChange?.()`.
- A "Retry" action button that re-runs the same parse+merge+split logic against the COMBINED content of both textareas, moving any now-valid lines into the primary box and leaving/returning still-invalid ones in the errors box.

Write tests for: opening the modal; a successful all-valid-lines import merges into state and clears the primary textarea (or leaves it — your call, document it, e.g. maybe it's more useful to clear after a successful import so the box is ready for the next paste; pick one and pin it with a test); a mixed valid/invalid input splits correctly (valid lines' effects appear in `getState()`, invalid lines' raw text ends up in the errors textarea, and some human-readable error info is present); pressing Retry after fixing one previously-bad line (edit the errors textarea's value in the test, then click Retry) results in that line moving into the primary box and being merged into state, while a still-bad line remains in the errors box.

- Real DOM APIs only, no `innerHTML` with interpolated untrusted content — use `createElement`/`textContent` (matches the security pattern already established in `matrix-interactions.ts`/`forms.ts`).
- Strict TS, no `any`.
- Don't modify `import-parser.ts`, `model.ts`, `actions.ts`, `render-decisions.ts`, `forms.ts`, `matrix-interactions.ts`, or their tests — only import from them. If `forms.ts` doesn't export something you need (e.g. the attractor id-generation helper), write your own equivalent in your new file rather than modifying `forms.ts`.
- Stub functions throw `new Error("not yet implemented — green phase")`.

Run `cd web && nix develop /home/v0id/Documents/repos/residual -c bun test` and confirm the 128 pre-existing tests still pass unchanged, and your new tests fail via the intended stub throw. Keep prose under 500 words plus signatures/output.

```ts
function applyAddForce(state: PendingState, kind: "stressor" | "purpose", item: PendingItem): PendingState {
  const { state: withRow, tempId } = addForceRow(state, kind);
  let next = withRow;
  for (const [flagName, value] of Object.entries(item.fields)) {
    const field = FORCE_FIELD_MAP[flagName];
    if (field === undefined) continue;
    next = updateForceField(next, tempId, field, value);
  }
  next = applyComponentToggles(next, tempId, item);
  return next;
}

function applyAddComponent(state: PendingState, item: PendingItem): PendingState {
  return addComponentColumn(state, {
    name: item.fields.name ?? "",
    description: item.fields.description ?? "",
    status: (item.fields.status as "proposed" | "actual") ?? "proposed",
    architectureSet: item.fields["architecture-set"] ?? "",
  });
}

function applyAddAttractor(state: PendingState, item: PendingItem): PendingState {
  const id = nextAttractorId(state);
  return addAttractorOption(state, {
    id,
    name: item.fields.name ?? "",
    description: item.fields.description ?? "",
    positiveState: item.fields["positive-state"] ?? "",
    negativeState: item.fields["negative-state"] ?? "",
  });
}

function applyUpdateForce(state: PendingState, item: PendingItem): PendingState {
  const forceKey = item.fields["force-id"];
  if (forceKey === undefined) return state;
  let next = state;
  for (const [flagName, value] of Object.entries(item.fields)) {
    if (flagName === "force-id") continue;
    const field = FORCE_FIELD_MAP[flagName];
    if (field === undefined) continue;
    next = updateForceField(next, forceKey, field, value);
  }
  next = applyComponentToggles(next, forceKey, item);
  return next;
}

function isMergeable(item: PendingItem): boolean {
  if (item.kind === "add") {
    return item.type === "stressor" || item.type === "purpose" || item.type === "component" || item.type === "attractor";
  }
  return item.type === "stressor" || item.type === "purpose";
}

function applyItem(state: PendingState, item: PendingItem): PendingState {
  if (item.kind === "add") {
    if (item.type === "stressor" || item.type === "purpose") return applyAddForce(state, item.type, item);
    if (item.type === "component") return applyAddComponent(state, item);
    if (item.type === "attractor") return applyAddAttractor(state, item);
  }
  return applyUpdateForce(state, item);
}

export function mergeImportedItems(state: PendingState, items: PendingItem[]): MergeResult {
  let next = state;
  const unmergeable: PendingItem[] = [];
  for (const item of items) {
    if (!isMergeable(item)) { unmergeable.push(item); continue; }
    next = applyItem(next, item);
  }
  return { state: next, unmergeable };
}
```

```ts
interface ImportErrorEntry { line: string; message: string; }

function requireElement<T extends Element>(container: HTMLElement, selector: string): T {
  const el = container.querySelector(selector);
  if (el === null) throw new Error(`mountImportModal: missing required element ${selector}`);
  return el as T;
}

export function mountImportModal(
  container: HTMLElement,
  getState: () => PendingState,
  setState: (next: PendingState) => void,
  options?: MountImportModalOptions,
): void {
  const trigger = requireElement<HTMLElement>(container, "[data-import-trigger]");
  const modal = requireElement<HTMLElement>(container, "[data-import-modal]");
  const primary = requireElement<HTMLTextAreaElement>(container, "[data-import-primary]");
  const errorsBox = requireElement<HTMLTextAreaElement>(container, "[data-import-errors]");
  const errorList = requireElement<HTMLElement>(container, "[data-import-error-list]");
  const runButton = requireElement<HTMLElement>(container, "[data-import-run]");
  const retryButton = requireElement<HTMLElement>(container, "[data-import-retry]");

  const renderErrors = (entries: ImportErrorEntry[]): void => {
    errorsBox.value = entries.map((e) => e.line).join("\n");
    while (errorList.firstChild) errorList.removeChild(errorList.firstChild);
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const li = document.createElement("li");
      li.textContent = `${entry.line}: ${entry.message}`;
      errorList.appendChild(li);
    }
  };

  const processImportText = (text: string): ImportErrorEntry[] => {
    const parsed = parseImportText(text);
    const mergeResult = mergeImportedItems(getState(), parsed.items);
    setState(mergeResult.state);
    return [
      ...parsed.errors.map((e): ImportErrorEntry => ({ line: e.line, message: e.message })),
      ...mergeResult.unmergeable.map((item): ImportErrorEntry => ({
        line: item.raw,
        message: `no support yet for "${item.kind} ${item.type}" updates`,
      })),
    ];
  };

  trigger.addEventListener("click", () => modal.removeAttribute("hidden"));

  runButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
    renderErrors(processImportText(primary.value));
    primary.value = "";
    options?.onChange?.();
  });

  retryButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
    renderErrors(processImportText(`${primary.value}\n${errorsBox.value}`));
    primary.value = "";
    options?.onChange?.();
  });
}
```

```ts
// DOM-wiring layer restoring the matrix-view interactions that used to live
// in an inline <script> in src/view/shell.html (live text filter, click-to-
// sort headers, accordion expand/collapse, fusion/fission threshold
// highlighting). That inline script was deleted wholesale while wiring in
// the new TS-based live-editing system (Phases 0-8 of
// residual/iterations/view-live-editing-plan.md) and never reimplemented —
// this module is the fix for that regression.
//
// [... header comment unchanged from stub ...]

export interface MatrixViewOptions {
  onChange?: () => void;
}

export interface MatrixViewHandle {
  recomputeFusionFission: () => void;
}

type SortDir = "asc" | "desc";

function sortMatrixBy(container: HTMLElement, key: string, dir: SortDir): void {
  const table = container.querySelector("table.matrix");
  const tbody = table?.querySelector("tbody");
  if (!tbody) return;
  const rows = Array.from(tbody.querySelectorAll<HTMLTableRowElement>("tr.force-row"));
  const mult = dir === "desc" ? -1 : 1;

  rows.sort((ra, rb) => {
    if (key === "force") {
      return (ra.getAttribute("data-force-id") ?? "").localeCompare(rb.getAttribute("data-force-id") ?? "") * mult;
    }
    if (key === "total") {
      return (Number(ra.getAttribute("data-row-total") ?? 0) - Number(rb.getAttribute("data-row-total") ?? 0)) * mult;
    }
    if (key.indexOf("component:") === 0) {
      const comp = key.slice("component:".length);
      const ca = ra.querySelector(`td[data-component="${CSS.escape(comp)}"]`);
      const cb = rb.querySelector(`td[data-component="${CSS.escape(comp)}"]`);
      const va = ca?.getAttribute("data-coupled") === "1" ? 1 : 0;
      const vb = cb?.getAttribute("data-coupled") === "1" ? 1 : 0;
      return (va - vb) * mult;
    }
    return 0;
  });

  for (const row of rows) tbody.appendChild(row);
}

interface FusionFissionResult {
  fusion: Set<string>;
  fission: Set<string>;
}

function computeMatrixCandidates(container: HTMLElement): FusionFissionResult {
  const table = container.querySelector("table.matrix");
  const fusion = new Set<string>();
  const fission = new Set<string>();
  if (!table) return { fusion, fission };

  const componentNames = Array.from(table.querySelectorAll("thead th[data-component]")).map(
    (th) => th.getAttribute("data-component") ?? "",
  );

  const vectors: Record<string, Record<string, boolean>> = {};
  for (const name of componentNames) vectors[name] = {};

  for (const td of Array.from(table.querySelectorAll("tbody td[data-residue-cell]"))) {
    const comp = td.getAttribute("data-component") ?? "";
```

content.text:
All 8 phases of the live-editing feature are complete and committed — 15 commits on top of `9ad1ff3`, everything green (Rust: 309+4+5+30 tests; TS: 185 tests via `bun test` against a real DOM; `residual verify all` passes; clippy clean on touched files; manual smoke test confirms the rendered page has no unresolved placeholders and no network calls).

**What landed:**
- `residual update` CLI subcommand (previously didn't exist) for mutating existing stressors/purposes/attractors/components/terms/personas, with `--add-component`/`--remove-component` folding NKP mutation in
- A hidden `residual internal cli-schema` command so the TS import parser stays in parity with real CLI flags automatically, not by hand-maintained duplication
- Full client-side live-editing: double-click to toggle NKP cells, right-click to add rows (opening straight into edit mode), Edit/OK/Cancel for non-NKP fields with an attractor dropdown, add-component-as-column, proposed/unrelated visibility toggles, red invalid-row/cell highlighting distinct from the existing fusion/fission treatment
- Bidirectional CLI text: paste `residual add/update` commands back into the UI via an Import modal, with failed lines split into a retry-able errors box
- "Generate bash script" download (shebang + `residual write authorize` header + commands) alongside the existing plain copy
- All of it tested against a real DOM via happy-dom (169+ TS tests), not left as browser-only manual verification

**Two things worth knowing about:**
1. I found and fixed a real bug mid-flight: a freshly-added stressor/purpose has no `--force-id` until `add stressor` actually runs and prints one, so the original design would have generated scripts referencing a fake ID. Fixed via shell-variable capture (`NEW_1_ID=$(residual add stressor ... | grep ...)`).
2. The final integration pass initially deleted the old inline script's filter/sort/accordion-toggle/fusion-fission-threshold behavior without replacing it — a real regression, caught before it landed and fixed by porting that logic faithfully into a new tested `matrix-view.ts` module before I committed anything.

Branch `tdd-implement/defense-ledger-proposed-components` is 16 commits ahead of wherever it started this session, still uncommitted-nothing outstanding — working tree is clean.
